isolation: Service1 is stateless and API-only; each scenario is asserted directly against its own HTTP response, with no shared container to isolate. Service2's catalog mode is global, mutable state owned entirely by service2 — but service2 has exposure "intranet" per specs/design/components/service2/design.json and no endpoint for it was provided in /tmp/validation-context.json (only service1's internet-exposed endpoint was given). This run never guessed or probed for a service2 URL, so it had no interface to set, reset, or even read the catalog mode directly, and no way to isolate that state from whatever else may be acting on the shared deployment.

scenarios.rule: The average score is the sum of every record's score divided by the record count, discarded to a whole number

steps.text: the catalog is in full mode
steps.observed: No interface was available to set or verify service2's catalog mode directly: service2 is intranet-only per its design.json and no URL for it was provided. Service1's own /average-score response is the only indirect signal, and it never showed full-mode behaviour: early in the run it alternated between 503 "no healthy upstream" / connection-refused (service1 itself unreachable) and one 500 " / by zero" (consistent with an empty catalog crashing an unguarded division); once service1 stabilized it returned a steady {"average":0}, which is empty-mode behaviour, not full mode. The precondition could not be established and the live state contradicts it.

scenarios.rule: A request to a path Service1 does not serve returns a structured 404 body
scenarios.scenario: Requesting a path Service1 does not serve

steps.observed: After an initial unhealthy period (503 "no healthy upstream" / connection refused for roughly the first 15 minutes of this run, see the average-score scenario's evidence), service1 stabilized and returned HTTP 404, confirming it is up and answering requests.

steps.text: Alex the API Consumer requests the path "/unknown-path" from Service1
steps.observed: HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found, content-type: application/json, reproduced identically across 2 separate calls.

steps.text: Alex receives a structured 404 error body
steps.observed: {"code":404, "message":"Not Found", "description":"No resource exists for the path '/unknown-path'"} — a structured object with code, message and description fields, matching the Error schema shape documented in specs/design/components/service2/openapi.yaml and service1's own description of returning a structured 404 body.
